metaDescription: Free online XML formatter. Pretty-print XML with your choice of indent, keep or drop comments, and preserve mixed content. Runs in your browser.
intro: Pretty-print XML with consistent indentation. Elements, attributes, CDATA and the XML declaration are kept, mixed text content is preserved, and comments can be kept or removed.
why:
XML from a SOAP response, an RSS feed or an export is often delivered on a single line. That makes it nearly impossible to see which element contains which, or where a closing tag is missing. A formatter lays the tree out so you can read it.

The tool re-indents elements, keeps attributes and CDATA sections, and treats text mixed with tags, like a paragraph with a bold word, carefully so that spacing in the text is not changed. You choose 2, 4 or 8 spaces or a tab, and whether comments stay. Malformed XML is reported rather than guessed at. Formatting happens in your browser and nothing is uploaded, which matters when the XML contains customer records.
howTo: Paste your XML into the input box.
Choose the indent: 2, 4 or 8 spaces, or a tab.
Tick Keep comments if you want comments retained.

faq.a: Whitespace between elements is rearranged, but text content is not altered. Where text and tags are mixed, as in an element containing text and a child, the original spacing is preserved.

faq.q: What if the XML is not well-formed?
faq.a: The tool reports an error instead of producing output. Use the XML Validator for a clear check of well-formedness using the browser parser.

faq.q: Are CDATA sections and comments kept?
faq.a: CDATA sections are kept as they are. Comments are kept when the option is ticked and removed when it is not.

faq.q: Can it format XML with namespaces?
faq.a: Namespace prefixes and declarations are kept as written. The tool re-indents; it does not resolve or validate namespaces or check against a DTD or schema.
